transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-06
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Avery (Redwood AE), Samir (Redwood SE), Maya (Redwood CSM), Elena (VerdantCare Head of MLOps), Marcus (VP Eng), Priya (DevOps), Tom (Procurement), Nadia (QA)

Summary: quick renewal/retainer discussion, scope EU private pilot + APAC readout, confirm SSO/KMS and pricing tradeoffs.

[00:00] Avery (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — can you state names and roles?
[00:08] Elena: Elena Ruiz, head of MLOps at VerdantCare. Hey.
[00:10] Marcus: Marcus Lee, VP engineering.
[00:12] Priya: Priya Anand, DevOps.
[00:14] Tom: Tom Berger, procurement.
[00:16] Nadia: Nadia, QA.
[00:18] Avery: Great. From Redwood, Samir, Maya and I. Appreciate you carving this time out. We put together an agenda: renewal sizing, EU private pilot timeline, APAC onboarding cadence, security/KMS questions and then next steps.

[00:34] Samir (Redwood SE): I'll try to keep the technical bits short — or at least clear — and then Maya will cover some of the ops/CS items on retention and billing.

[00:42] Marcus: High level — we're broadly happy. Performance's been good in US. Now the ask is to expand to EU and APAC and get a predictable unit price. We've got a couple of internal stakeholders who want the VPC/private path for EU for regulatory reasons.

[00:58] Elena: Yeah and just to be explicit: EU requires data residency for PII-derived artifacts. We may need private serving there for some models. APAC could be hosted but prefer region-specific KMS and SSO.

[01:16] Priya: Also want to call out burst patterns — we have irregular peaks tied to release days, so the autoscale/burst behaviour matters to our cost.

[01:25] Avery: Understood. Let's pull usage — Marcus, do you have the last 30 days QPS and p95?

[01:32] Marcus: Quick numbers: average 18 QPS on text-gen endpoints, peak 82 QPS for short windows, p95 about 420ms on hosted Redwood model x86 profile. Token volumes about 1.2B tokens last month. Costs are creeping up.

[01:50] Samir: Helpful. So for EU private, we recommend a small dedicated pool to start — warm nodes + autoscaling threshold. That gives you isolation and predictable latency. The tradeoff is higher commitment and lead time for provisioning.

[02:05] Elena: What's the lead time? procurement wants a calendar.

[02:08] Samir: Typical EU private onprem or VPC: 4–6 weeks for network setup + certs + KMS integration; if you want on-prem air-gapped it's more like 6–10 weeks.

[02:20] Priya: Are those numbers assuming we provide connectivity details and firewalls up front?

[02:24] Samir: Yes — we need CIDR ranges, peering details, and a little firewall hole list (I'll share the exact ports). Also you'll need to decide between BYOK KMS vs Redwood-managed keys.

[02:34] Nadia: Quick Q — how does KV cache work across a dedicated pool? Is that shared between models?

[02:38] Samir: Good question. The kv cache is per-instance, per-model variant. Cache warmup is automated but prefix caching is supported; some clients use a shared cache layer in front for conversational workloads. Sorry, I said kv cash earlier in a doc — that was a typo in the deck, will fix.

[02:55] Marcus: Cost question — hosted + bursts vs dedicated reserved capacity. What's the unit delta?

[03:01] Maya (CSM): For your profile, short answer: hosted with burst is lower upfront but higher marginal for sustained token volume. Dedicated reserved reduces unit cost by ~25–35% depending on quantization and steady state. We'll run the numbers against your 1.2B tokens.

[03:18] Tom: On procurement timeline — we need a firm price table to compare vs the incumbent (MegaCloudAI).

[03:24] Avery: We'll send a revised commitment sheet. Action: I'll push a 12-month and 24-month pricing ladder with dedicated vs hosted comparisons.

[03:32] Tom: Great — include egress and support SLAs.

[03:35] Samir: Want to dig into performance SLOs: you said p95 ~420ms — is that for 2k context?

[03:40] Marcus: That's typically 1k–1.5k avg context. For longer sequences we see p95 up to 900ms.

[03:48] Samir: Ok, interesting — our EU private baseline can be optimized at deployment time by picking the right kernel set and sequence-length shaping. We'll propose quantization profiles too; for chat it's often q4_0 or int8-like paths.

[04:05] Elena: On security — we need SOC2 evidence, audit logs, and proof of KMS integration. Also SAML SSO for user provisioning.

[04:12] Maya: We have SOC2 Type II report that I can share (redacted). We also have audit log samples and our KMS guides for AWS KMS, HashiCorp Vault, and CloudHSM.

[04:22] Elena: Which vendors have other customers been using for KMS integration in EU?

[04:25] Samir: Most customers use AWS KMS (if they're in AWS), Google KMS in GCP, and some use HashiCorp Vault with a HSM backing. We'll share a short compatibility matrix.

[04:36] Priya: For SSO, we use Okta. Do you support Just-in-Time provisioning?

[04:40] Maya: Yes we support Okta SAML with SCIM provisioning; JIT is possible depending on the setup.

[04:45] Tom: Any vendor lock concerns? our security team asked about data export if we decide to leave.

[04:50] Avery: We provide data export tooling and a migration handoff plan; audit trails show data exfil and we can work with legal on retention terms. We'll include a clause in the SOW.

[05:00] [INTERLUDE - 5:00 to 12:00 — deeper technical dive led by Samir]
[05:08] Samir: For the EU private pilot, recommended architecture: a small dedicated pool of 2 A100-equivalent nodes (or T4x for lower-cost models) with a warm standby node for failover. Network: VPC peering with IP allowlist, NAT for outbound control, and mTLS for the control-plane channel. If you want on-prem, we'll use our private agent with cert-based auth.
[05:35] Marcus: Can you quantify the p50/p95 improvement from dedicated vs hosted?
[05:38] Samir: In our benchmarks for similar workloads we saw p95 drop from ~420–800ms hosted down to around ~220–340ms dedicated depending on model variant and batch sizing.
[05:50] Elena: What about caching and prefix reuse for our conversation flows? We have many short-turn convos that could benefit.
[05:55] Samir: That is exactly where batching + prefix cache saves tokens and reduces latency. We'll enable automatic prefix caching and suggest prompt templates to maximize reuse.
[06:05] Priya: Any caveats about model variants and fallbacks? We use a fine-tuned model in prod.
[06:09] Samir: You can pin a model version and have an automatic fallback to a compatible lighter quantized variant if capacity strained. That is part of the routing policy. There can be slight output distribution shifts — we recommend A/B evals on a sample prompt set.

[06:22] Nadia: QA question — how easy is it to replay traffic for regression?
[06:25] Samir: We have an eval harness you can run against a staging variant; you can replay logs to staging and we capture diffs plus a quality regression alerting pipeline.

[06:34] [Transcript noise / crosstalk]
[06:38] Speaker 1 (redacted): mmhmm, yep.

[06:42] Avery: Let's pivot to APAC. You said hosted would be acceptable there if we can get a regional KMS and lower egress.
[06:50] Marcus: Correct; APAC is lower priority but needs lower latency for Japan and Singapore. We want a plan to add APAC within Q2 if possible.

[06:58] Samir: APAC hosted spin-up is faster — we can enable region routing within 2–3 weeks once we confirm model variants and sizing. For private APAC, similar 4–6 weeks for VPC.

[07:12] Marcus: Regarding pricing, can we do a blended commitment? e.g., dedicated EU + hosted APAC with a single retainer?

[07:18] Maya: Absolutely — many customers do hybrid commitments. We'll produce a blended quote and show expected unit costs per token and per-embedding based on your volume mix.

[07:28] Tom: For contracting, we need examples of the SLA language, uptime, and credits.

[07:34] Avery: We'll include sample SLA language in the pricing packet. Typical is a 99.9% uptime for dedicated pools with defined latency SLOs and credit bands.

[07:42] Marcus: One more technical ask — we'd like to run a short stress test using our typical traffic shape against both hosted and a dedicated staging cluster to compare p95. Is that feasible?

[07:50] Samir: Yes. We can do a two-hour soak test in staging and give you the traces. We ask for a small credit for soak capacity but usually it's covered under pilot credits.

[08:02] Elena: Timing wise — if we sign a 12-month commitment by mid-March can we target EU private pilot in April?

[08:09] Avery: If procurement signs by Mar 15 and network info is provided same week, April pilot is feasible. That's roughly a 4–6 week path.

[08:18] Tom: Procurement will need PO templates and invoice cadence.

[08:22] Maya: We'll attach PO templates and standard invoice schedules. Also offer monthly or quarterly billing for commitments depending on financial approval.

[08:30] [12:00–30:00 minute block — practical clarifications and off-mic sidebars captured] 
[12:05] Priya: On the KMS integration, if we pick HashiCorp Vault, is there an example playbook?

[12:11] Samir: Yes — Samir: we'll share a Vault playbook including service accounts, policies, and rotation guidance.

[12:20] Nadia: For QA — will the staging logs contain PII? We need redaction guidance.

[12:24] Maya: We recommend synthetic or redacted datasets for staging. We also provide a log redaction utility for the replay harness.

[12:33] Marcus: About fallbacks — if EU private pool saturates in high traffic, will traffic route automatically to hosted region and does that break data residency?

[12:41] Samir: Routing fallback is policy driven. You can configure fallback to a compatible private pool in another EU region; automatic routing to hosted will only happen if you opt-in — and it'll be flagged in audit logs. We'll ensure the default is not to route outside EU without an explicit opt-in.

[12:57] Avery: Good catch. We'll make sure the SOW includes the routing policy language about residency and fallback.

[13:04] Tom: Any compliance gaps we should know about?

[13:07] Maya: Nothing major. We'll provide SOC2 Type II, DPIA notes, and our data handling docs. For country-specific legal requirements in the EU, we recommend you loop in your legal counsel but we have precedent customers who did similar onboarding.

[13:20] [Final 10 minutes — recap and next steps]
[13:22] Avery: Quick recap: 1) Redwood to send updated pricing (12/24 month) and SLA examples — Avery will send by 2026-03-10. 2) Samir to share EU private checklist, ports, and Vault playbook by 2026-03-12. 3) Maya to share SOC2 cert and audit log sample by 2026-03-09. 4) VerdantCare to confirm KMS vendor and SSO provider by 2026-03-18. 5) Schedule a staging soak test week of Mar 22 pending signatures.

[13:56] Elena: That timeline works. For procurement I'll follow up but we want the price grid sooner rather than later.

[14:02] Tom: We'll aim to review pricing and get internal signatures. I will own the PO.

[14:06] Marcus: We'll collect the QPS traces and p95 targets and send to Samir by 2026-03-08.

[14:12] Priya: I'll coordinate DevOps side and provide network CIDR and peering contacts.

[14:16] Avery: Awesome. Anything else?
[14:18] Elena: Small ask — can you include a short note about how quantization might affect output quality? We want to understand tradeoffs.

[14:24] Samir: Yes — I'll include a 1-page summary with recommended quant profiles and expected token savings vs small output delta.

[14:31] Avery: Thanks all. We'll follow up with the docs and a calendar invite for the pilot planning session.

[14:38] [meeting ends, 48 minutes total, recording stopped]

Notes on transcription: occasional names mis-typed by auto-transcript (e.g., 'kv cash' instead of 'kv cache'). Some overlap and brief speaker labelling errors.
